item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission investigated possible serious misconduct by public officers at the Shire of Halls Creek.
item.support: Operation Oakley was an investigation commenced by the Commission to determine whether any public officer employed by or elected to the Shire

item.text: Its inquiries covered recruitment, outside business interests, leave entitlements and vehicle procurement.
item.support: from the appointment of Ms Little, to his own private business interests and the management of a Shire tender

item.text: The Commission formed a serious misconduct opinion about the chief executive officer's appointment of his partner.
item.support: The Commission has formed an opinion of serious misconduct in respect of Mr Kerr-Newell's appointment of Ms Little.

item.text: It concluded that insufficient oversight had allowed the chief executive officer to use Shire resources for private benefit.
item.support: Mr Kerr-Newell's tenure went relatively unchecked which enabled him to take advantage of the Shire's resources for his own private benefit.

item.text: The Commission stressed fair tender processes and procurement knowledge among staff responsible for Shire finances.
item.support: Councils must ensure that those who have any role in Shire finances are well-versed in procurement processes
